newsitem.title: USA: Schult Homes sees weather hurting FY97 Q3.
newsitem.headline: Schult Homes sees weather hurting FY97 Q3.

text.p: Shult Homes Corp said Thursday winter weather should hurt demand for mobile homes in the fiscal 1997 third quarter, ending in March, more than it has in the milder winters the past two years.

"This year we are experiencing a 'normal' winter with all the images of bad weather that thought implies," Schult chief executive Walter Wells said in a news release. "As a result, consumer activity has also dipped as it normally does at this time of year. Thus, we expect our performance in the third quarter to be relatively flat relative to a year ago, with the gains fueled by enhanced productivity to be offset by relatively slower sales."
The company reported net income of $829,000, or $0.22 in the third quarter of fiscal 1996 on revenues of $71.7 million.
"We will be making some changes in the mix we produce at various plants to further enhance our performance over the next year," Wells said.
Earlier Thursday, Schult reported net income of $1.8 million, or $0.47 a share in the second quarter, up from $1.2 million, or $0.31 a share a year ago.
